To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

employee commitment to an organization, a supervisor, and a job are all related to discretionary work behavior, that these relationships are mediated by goal regulation, and that goal regulation is related to discretionary work effort through the mediating variables of intrinsic motivation and self efficacy.

The more an individual identifies with, is involved in, and is committed to a job, organization, or supervisor, the more likely he or she will engage in discretionary work behaviors that are beneficial to the organization.

the effects of employee commitment on work outcomes depend on the motivational processes that link commitment to behavior, and the motivational processes that are most likely to occur depend on the form of commitment, the focus of commitment, and the basis of commitment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the various forms, foci and bases of commitment interact with the motivational processes of goal regulation to affect the quality and quantity of discretionary work behavior.

the question of how employees' work-related commitments affect the quality of their work performance, and the extent to which this relationship is moderated by employees' goal regulations and regulatory foci.
how employees can be motivated to commit to their work, how they can be motivated to perform discretionary work behavior, and how these two processes can be linked.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the employee's commitment to the organization and the job is an important factor that affects the motivation of the employee and in turn the employee's performance.

commitment and motivation have been studied separately, with little or no cross-fertilization of ideas and findings, and that a more integrated approach to the study of commitment and motivation is needed.
the relationship between employee commitment and employee motivation is a positive one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
commitment and motivation are both energizing forces, but that commitment has a special role in the motivation process.

the model of goal regulation and commitment provides a conceptual foundation for the integration of commitment and motivation research and a framework that can be used to generate new research and test existing theories.
employee commitment and motivation are not mutually exclusive concepts, and that they are better understood when they are integrated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the motivational and commitment literatures can be brought together to provide a more complete and useful understanding of the energizing forces underlying work behavior.
commitment and motivation are not distinct phenomena.
employee commitment is one form of goal regulation.
